extracted.intended_audience: District of Columbia rulemaking authorities (Office of Documents, agencies), Council staff, and members of the public who submit or manage public comments
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural requirements for how proposed rules in the District of Columbia must accept and publish public comments, including electronic submission and maintenance of a directory, and the fiscal/applicability steps triggering the act's operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must permit both oral and written comments and electronic submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment to Section 105(a) (D.C. Official Code § 2-505(a)): replaces prior phrasing with: "both orally and in writing. The notice shall provide for electronic submission of written data and views in all instances."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All notices of documents published in the D.C. Register that require a public comment period must state that comments may be submitted both orally and in writing, and must explicitly provide for electronic submission of written comments in every instance. (This replaces language that allowed either oral or written as specified.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Documents must publish and maintain an electronic directory of proposed rules open for public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: New subsection (j) to Section 303 (D.C. Official Code § 2-553): "The District of Columbia Office of Documents shall publish and maintain an electronic directory of all proposed rules open for public comment under this act."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office of Documents is required to create and continuously maintain an electronic directory listing all proposed rules that are currently open for public comment under the Administrative Procedure Act, ensuring public access and discoverability of open rulemakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability tied to inclusion of fiscal effect in approved budget and financial plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Sec. 3(a): "This act shall apply upon the date of inclusion of its fiscal effect in an approved budget and financial plan."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The act does not automatically take effect on enactment; its applicability begins when its fiscal effect has been included in an approved budget and financial plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief Financial Officer must certify inclusion date and notify Budget Director
rubrics_metrics.description: Sec. 3(b): "The Chief Financial Officer shall certify the date of the inclusion of the fiscal effect in an approved budget and financial plan, and provide notice to the Budget Director of the Council of the certification."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal certification by the CFO is required to identify the effective inclusion date of the fiscal effect; the CFO must notify the Council's Budget Director so the procedural trigger for applicability is documented and communicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Director must publish notice of CFO certification in the D.C. Register; publication date does not affect applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Sec. 3(c)(1)-(2): "The Budget Director shall cause the notice of the certification to be published in the District of Columbia Register. (2) The date of publication of the notice of the certification shall not affect the applicability of this act."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After CFO certification, the Budget Director is responsible for publishing that certification notice in the D.C. Register for public record; however, the act's applicability is determined by the CFO's certification date (inclusion in budget), not by the date the notice is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council adopts committee report fiscal impact statement as required fiscal impact statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Sec. 4: "The Council adopts the fiscal impact statement in the committee report as the fiscal impact statement required by section 4a of the General Legislative Procedures Act of 1975..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute incorporates the committee report's fiscal impact statement to satisfy statutory requirements for fiscal impact reporting; rule drafters and analysts should refer to the committee report for the official fiscal impact statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date contingent on mayoral approval (or Council override) and 30-day congressional review
rubrics_metrics.description: Sec. 5: "This act shall take effect following approval by the Mayor (or in the event of veto by the Mayor, action by the Council to override the veto) and a 30-day period of congressional review as provided in section 602(c)(1) of the District of Columbia Home Rule Act..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The act becomes effective only after (1) mayoral approval or Council override of a veto and (2) the completion of the 30-day congressional review period under the Home Rule Act. Practitioners should track these conditions to determine when the statute's requirements become operative.
